00 · What Changed

Why accuracy was low, and what actually fixed it

The original 4-class model (None/Mild/Moderate/Severe) scored ~49% accuracy. Grid-searching harder wouldn't have fixed that — a Cohen's d effect-size analysis showed Moderate vs. Severe differ by less than 0.16 standard deviations on every available feature, meaning the two labels are statistically indistinguishable in this dataset. v2 merges them into a data-driven "High" class, then applies real GridSearchCV across Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and HistGradientBoosting for both prediction tasks.

01 · GridSearchCV Model Selection

Best model chosen per task, not assumed

Each task ran a 5-fold cross-validated grid search over 3 algorithms; the best performer by weighted F1 was selected automatically.

03 · Personalization

Behavioral personas (K-Means)

Users are grouped into five personas based on how they actually spend screen time.

Persona distribution

Behavior flag frequency

Balanced User 1,906 users · 25.4%

Usage is well distributed across work, rest, and downtime.

Night Owl / Sleep-Deprived 1,815 users · 24.2%

High screen time paired with short sleep. Sleep hygiene is the highest-leverage fix.

Social Media Heavy User 1,375 users · 18.3%

Social apps dominate usage. App-level time limits help most here.

Gaming-Heavy User 1,297 users · 17.3%

Gaming dominates screen time. Time-boxing sessions protects study/work hours.

Fragmented Attention User 1,107 users · 14.8%

High notification load and app-switching. Focus sessions rebuild attention span.

04 · Try It

Look up any user's personalized wellness report

Search by user ID (e.g. U00001–U07500) to see their individual risk prediction and persona.

Digital Wellness Analyzer v2 — dataset: Smartphone Usage & Addiction Analysis (7,500 users). Models: GridSearchCV-tuned RandomForest (addiction risk), RandomForest (risk level), Isolation Forest (anomaly detection), K-Means (persona segmentation). See README for the full effect-size analysis behind merging Moderate/Severe into "High".
